judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Practical, plot-bound instructions (secret route, bookcases open) and a plain off-screen death folded into the next errand read like a chapter hub; the em-dash and 'Unsavory elements dwell in the shadows!' are period Westwood.

items.label: B
items.critique: Hits every slot neatly (theft, place, reward, pass, guards) with a stock 'Ah! A capable soul, at last!' and 'grievous crime'; the 'Oh.... You do not have it.' reminder looks borrowed rather than earned.

items.label: C
items.critique: Slightly awkward, breathless child-like voice ('he'll be destroyed', 'Could you... would you') and a bare thanks with an unnamed token feel authentically uneven rather than designed.

items.label: D
items.critique: Overwrought pathos ('Useless! Useless!', weeping every night) and a tidy explanatory backstory are longer and more literary than Nox's townsfolk; the exact '80 gold pieces' reward echoes F.

items.label: E
items.critique: The startled 'Gahhhhhh! No! Don't kill me!', the half-blind misreading, '?!' punctuation and the oddly specific bat scroll for conjurers have Westwood's quirky humour and loose plotting.

items.label: F
items.critique: Crafted comic persona (wipe both feet, don't scratch the glass, hid under the bed) is a deliberate character bit; the callbacks are too neat and the reminder hint is phrased as a writer's tip.

items.label: G
items.critique: A single run-on paragraph as a characterization device is a modern writerly flourish Nox never uses; the thanks then reuses 'token of my appreciation' wholesale.

items.label: H
items.critique: Mayor's welcome, odd capitalization ('East', 'Urchins'), redundant directions ('located East of here', 'I should be in my house at the center of town') and the shop-then-Captain nudge are classic Westwood tutorial plainness.

items.label: I
items.critique: Grumpy-mourner opening and 'Those Imps bite' potion hand-off are a polished comic setup; 'darkest of times, with the [Person] beneath our feet' inserts lore in a way the originals rarely do, and the thanks is a stock copy.

items.label: J
items.critique: Begins mid-conversation ('Good!'), gives a ruby key and a petition with gruff brevity ('Have faith, one little urchin is no threat'); functional, unadorned, slightly flat in the Nox way.

tells: New texts give each giver a crafted comic or tragic persona (fussy, grieving, rambling, weeping); Westwood's givers are plainer and their humour comes from odd, unpolished moments rather than designed bits.
New texts reuse stock phrases lifted from the originals ('Oh.... You haven't got it', 'Please accept this as a token of my appreciation') and repeat exact rewards (80 gold) across texts.
Westwood lines carry practical logistics and quirks: where to go next, whom to see, odd capitalization, redundant directions, rewards that are items or passes tied to the plot.
Stylistic set pieces (a one-sentence run-on monologue, 'Useless! Useless!', tidy callbacks between offer and thanks) read as modern writerly technique, not Nox's register.
New offers bundle full backstory plus theft plus location plus reward plus question in one balanced speech; Westwood's are less evenly structured.
